explanation: The K101E mutation eliminates a positively charged lysine at the NNRTI pocket rim and replaces it with a negatively charged glutamate, reversing the local electrostatic environment and eliminating a potential cation-π or electrostatic interaction that stabilizes etravirine binding. The accompanying reduction in side-chain volume (−30.2 Ų) creates a binding cavity defect near the ligand contact interface (2.7 Å minimum distance), disrupting van der Waals contacts that normally contribute favorable binding interactions. This combination of electrostatic disruption and loss of favorable nonpolar contacts destabilizes the ETR-RT complex by approximately 1.3 kcal/mol, reducing inhibitor potency despite the mutation's position at the pocket periphery.
